name: Jumping Man
description: You have a tree rooted at node $$$1$$$ with $$$n$$$ nodes. Each node has a lowercase English letter written on it. For each integer $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, please solve the following problem independently: Consider the set of strings formed by the following process: Choose any node $$$u$$$ that is in the subtree of $$$i$$$ as your starting location. Repeat 0 or more times: Suppose you are currently on node $$$x$$$. Select a node $$$v$$$ that is in the subtree$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ of node $$$x$$$, but you may not choose $$$v=x$$$. Move to node $$$v$$$. This process can be terminated at any point. The characters obtained from all nodes you passed through (in order) are concatenated to form a string. You performed the above process exactly once for every possible path. Two paths are considered different if one node is visited in one path but not another. Now, you have obtained many strings. You want to know the sum of the square of the number of occurrences for each type of string. Since this answer might be very large, output its value modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A node $$$v$$$ is in another node $$$x$$$'s subtree if and only if the shortest path from node $$$1$$$ to node $$$v$$$ passes through node $$$x$$$.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 5000$$$). The description of the test cases follows. For each test case, the first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 5000$$$). The next line is a string of length $$$n$$$ containing only lowercase English letters, where the $$$i$$$-th character represents the letter on the $$$i$$$-th node. This is followed by $$$n-1$$$ lines, each containing two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \leq u,v \leq n, u \neq v$$$) representing an edge of the tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5000$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output $$$n$$$ numbers on a new line: the answer for $$$i=1,2,\ldots,n$$$, modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2183F — Jumping Man [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
